{{Short description|Closed flat 3-manifold}}
The '''Hantzsche–Wendt manifold''', also known as the '''HW manifold''' or '''didicosm''',<ref name="rossetti">{{cite journal |last1=Rossetti |first1=Juan P. |last2=Szczepański |first2=Andrzej |title=Generalized Hantzsche-Wendt flat manifolds |journal=Revista Matemática Iberoamericana |date=2005 |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=1053–1070 |doi=10.4171/RMI/445 |url=https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/4973|arxiv=math/0208205|s2cid=8222899 }}</ref> is a [[compact space|compact]], [[orientable]], [[flat manifold|flat]] [[3-manifold]], first studied by [[Walter Hantzsche]] and Hilmar Wendt in 1934.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hantzsche|first1=Walter|last2=Wendt|first2=Hilmar|date=1935|title=Dreidimensionale euklidische Raumformen|url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/bf01448045|journal=Mathematische Annalen|volume=110|issue=1|pages=593–611|doi=10.1007/bf01448045|s2cid=119961050 |issn=0025-5831|url-access=subscription}}</ref> It is the only closed flat 3-manifold with first [[Betti number]] zero. Its [[holonomy group]] is <math>\mathbb{Z}_2^2</math>.<ref name="miatello">{{cite journal |last1=Miatello |first1=R. J. |last2=Rossetti |first2=J. P. |title=Isospectral Hantzsche-Wendt manifolds |journal=Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik (Crelle's Journal) |date=29 October 1999 |volume=1999 |issue=515 |pages=1–23 |doi=10.1515/crll.1999.077 |url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/crll.1999.077/html |language=en |issn=1435-5345|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It has been suggested as a possible [[shape of the universe]] because its complicated topology can obscure the features in the [[cosmic microwave background]] that would arise if the universe is a closed [[flat manifold]], such as the [[3-torus]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Aurich |first1=R |last2=Lustig |first2=S |title=The Hantzsche–Wendt manifold in cosmic topology |journal=Classical and Quantum Gravity |date=21 August 2014 |volume=31 |issue=16 |article-number=165009 |doi=10.1088/0264-9381/31/16/165009 |arxiv=1403.2190 |bibcode=2014CQGra..31p5009A |s2cid=119223504 |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0264-9381/31/16/165009 |issn=0264-9381}}</ref>

==Construction==
[[File:Hantzsche–Wendt construction.svg|thumb|The Hantzsche–Wendt manifold is made from two cubes stacked on top of each other by gluing the identically-marked faces such that the markings line up.<ref name="flatori3">{{cite book |last=Demianski |first=Marek |title=The early universe and the cosmic microwave background: theory and observations |work= |publisher=Kluwer Academic Publishers |year=2003 |isbn=978-1-4020-1800-8 |editor-last=Sanchez |editor-first=Norma |editor-link=Norma Sanchez |location=Dordrecht |pages=166–169 |chapter=Topology of the universe and the cosmic microwave background radiation |editor-last2=Parijskij |editor-first2=Yuri}}</ref>]]
The HW manifold can be built from two cubes that share a face. One construction proceeds as follows:<ref name="flatori3"/>
# The top and bottom faces are glued to one another.
# One of the remaining sides is glued to the opposite side with a 180° rotation.
# One of the remaining faces on the top cube is glued to the matching face of the bottom cube, reflected across an axis parallel to the long axis of the double-cube.
# Repeat step 3 for the remaining pair of faces.

==Generalizations==
In addition to the orientable one (the Hantzsche–Wendt manifold), there are two non-orientable flat 3-manifolds with holonomy group <math>\mathbb{Z}_2^2</math>, known as the '''first''' and '''second amphidicosms''', both with first Betti number 1.<ref name="rossetti"/>

Similar flat ''n''-dimensional manifolds with holonomy <math>\mathbb{Z}_2^{n-1}</math>, known as '''generalized Hantzsche–Wendt manifolds''', may be constructed for any ''n''≥2, but orientable ones exist only in odd dimensions.<ref name="rossetti"/> The number of orientable HW manifolds up to [[diffeomorphism]] increases exponentially with dimension.<ref name="miatello"/> All of these have first Betti number ''β''<sub>1</sub> 0 or 1.<ref name="rossetti"/>
